_comment: Maps reference categories to the roles that read them. A role's reference chain is: authoring/references/roles/<role>.md, then authoring/references/categories/<id>.md for each category listing the role, then voice.md. required_roles (plan decision 22) are the roles that should not be considered configured without at least one reference level plus voice.md.

categories.label: Concept, premise and tone
categories.description: References for the central idea, intended experience, themes and atmosphere.

categories.label: Worldbuilding and history
categories.description: References for layered history, geography, institutions and believable places.

categories.label: Magic and power systems
categories.description: References for rules, limits, costs, interactions and social consequences of power.

categories.label: Cultures, factions and everyday life
categories.description: References for communities, institutions, belief, economy and lived material culture.

categories.label: Characters and fiction
categories.description: References for characterization, relationships, viewpoint, story structure and dialogue.

categories.label: Description and exposition
categories.description: References for conveying unfamiliar places, people, cultures and ideas through original prose.

categories.label: Geography and ecology
categories.description: An optional focused reference for physical landscapes, climate, resources and habitats.

categories.label: History and chronology
categories.description: An optional focused reference for causality, dating, contested accounts and historical layers.

categories.label: Belief and cosmology
categories.description: An optional focused reference for religions, metaphysics and differences between belief and truth.

categories.label: Economy and trade
categories.description: An optional focused reference for labor, ownership, infrastructure and exchange.

categories.label: Language and naming
categories.description: An optional focused reference for naming patterns, cultural contact and terminology.

categories.label: Creatures and ecology
categories.description: An optional reference for living creatures, habitats and interactions with society.

categories.label: Locations and settlements
categories.description: An optional focused reference for inhabitable places and their present-day pressures.

categories.label: Maps and spatial storytelling
categories.description: An optional reference for maps, scale, routes, legends and deliberate uncertainty.

categories.label: Environmental storytelling
categories.description: An optional reference for discoverable traces and fair inference from the environment.

categories.label: Lore and in-world documents
categories.description: An optional reference for situated documents, ambient details and attributed accounts.

categories.label: Knowledge and revelations
categories.description: An optional reference for how audiences learn, discover and reinterpret information.

categories.label: Quests and player agency
categories.description: An optional reference for player actions, branches and understandable consequences.

categories.label: Narrative systems and persistent state
categories.description: An optional reference for reactions, shared consequences and repeatable narrative behavior.

categories.label: Live events and ongoing arcs
categories.description: An optional reference for shared events, causal story waves and late participation.

categories.label: Player societies and emergent history
categories.description: An optional reference for collective player agency and evidence-based emergent history.

categories.label: Continuity and narrative review
categories.description: An optional reference for continuity methods and a specific review lens.
